title: Vietnam and Indonesia's Homegrown Sportswear Labels
seo_title: Vietnam and Indonesia's Homegrown Sportswear Labels
meta_description: Beyond Thailand's Grand Sport and Indonesia's League and Ortuseight running shoes -- the Vietnamese and Indonesian sportswear labels making running-specific kit.
dek: This site has already covered Thailand's Grand Sport, the Philippines' Recess, and Indonesia's League and Ortuseight running shoes. Here's a closer look at two brands that haven't come up yet: Vietnam's Kamito and Indonesia's Tiento and AUM Apparel.

sections.heading: Two Domestic Sportswear Scenes Growing in Different Directions
paragraphs: Vietnam and Indonesia have taken noticeably different paths to building homegrown sportswear brands. Indonesia's scene, covered elsewhere on this site through League and Ortuseight, grew up around running shoes first and expanded into apparel from there. Vietnam's path has run more through team sports -- football, badminton, pickleball -- with running as a newer addition to an already-established multi-sport catalog, which shapes what a Vietnamese sportswear brand's running range actually looks like today.

Both countries also have a second wave of smaller, design-forward labels sitting alongside the larger established names -- brands built around a specific city, community, or aesthetic rather than trying to cover every sport at once. That mix of scale and specialization is worth knowing about before assuming every local option is either a budget alternative or a niche curiosity.

sections.heading: Vietnam: Kamito's Multi-Sport Roots Into Running
paragraphs: Kamito was founded in 2018 by Midomax Vietnam, the country's exclusive Mizuno distributor, which is why it's sometimes described locally as "Vietnam's Mizuno" -- a brand built with real technical sportswear heritage rather than starting from casual wear. Based in Hanoi, it has grown into one of Vietnam's most recognized multi-sport labels, with dedicated ranges spanning football, badminton, table tennis, pickleball, and running, sold through its own online store with real Vietnamese-market pricing rather than imported markups.

A newer, smaller name worth knowing is Mude Sports, a Vietnam-based running, cycling, and triathlon apparel brand built around recycled polyester fabric made from plastic bottles. It sponsors and coaches Vietnamese elite trail runners rather than chasing mass-market volume, which places it at the opposite end of Vietnam's sportswear scene from a multi-sport catalog brand like Kamito -- smaller, more specialized, and more explicitly sustainability-focused.

sections.heading: Indonesia: Bandung's Tiento and Bali's AUM Apparel
paragraphs: Tiento was founded in 2013 in Bandung and, unlike Indonesia's better-known shoe-first brands, was built around apparel from the start -- baselayers, running jerseys, compression socks, leggings, running belts, and hats, used by Indonesian national athletes across multiple sports rather than positioned purely as running gear. Its catalog reads like a genuine technical sportswear line rather than general activewear with a running label attached.

AUM Apparel takes a different approach entirely. Founded in Bali in 2015 by Ni Made Dwi Agam Armini under the tagline "Mindfully Active," it builds sportswear -- leggings, sports bras, joggers, hoodies -- around designs drawn from Indonesian culture, including batik and ikat motifs. It's less a pure performance brand than Tiento or Kamito, but a genuinely distinct option for runners who want training kit that also reads as a piece of where it was made.

sections.heading: Why These Are Worth Seeking Out Over a Global Brand
paragraphs: The practical case is the same one that applies across the region's other local sportswear labels: prices well below imported technical apparel, sizing built for regional body types, and fabric choices already tuned for tropical heat rather than adapted from a brand designed in a cooler climate. None of these brands are trying to be a race-day technical wear replacement for a global performance label -- they're strongest as everyday training kit.

The more practical friction is availability -- like most of the region's homegrown labels, these sell primarily through their own domestic online stores and local marketplaces, with limited or no international shipping. The most reliable way to actually own one is buying directly during a race trip to Hanoi, Bandung, or Bali, rather than trying to order it in from outside the region.

products.name: Tiento Running Apparel

faqs.question: Is Kamito only a football brand, or does it make running gear too?
faqs.answer: Kamito started as a multi-sport brand founded by Mizuno's exclusive Vietnam distributor and has expanded into a dedicated running range, including its own FlyRun and Magic Run running shoes. Football remains a major part of its catalog, but running apparel and footwear are genuine, established product lines, not an afterthought.

faqs.question: How is Tiento different from Indonesia's League or Ortuseight?
faqs.answer: League and Ortuseight built their reputations around running shoes first. Tiento, founded in Bandung in 2013, was built around apparel from the start -- baselayers, running jerseys, leggings, and accessories used by Indonesian national athletes -- making it more of an apparel specialist than a footwear-first brand.

faqs.question: Can I buy Vietnamese or Indonesian local sportswear brands outside those countries?
faqs.answer: Mostly no -- these brands sell primarily through their own domestic online stores and local marketplaces, with limited or no international shipping. The most reliable way to actually own a piece is to buy it in person during a race trip to Hanoi, Bandung, or Bali.
